Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the evaluation kickoff (Sprint 0) and make the first two weeks high-velocity.

Recap (1-line): Syndexa is evaluating Redwood to reduce inference cost and hit 99th-percentile latency targets for document summarization use cases. Primary success criteria are: latency < 250ms p95 on typical queries and ~5-10% cost reduction vs current endpoint with acceptable answer quality.

Proposed Sprint 0 scope (draft):
- Week 0: Kickoff + alignment on success criteria, access, and initial prompt set
- Week 1: Tech deep-dive, sample data ingestion, run baseline evals
- Week 2: Prompt tuning + regressions check, handoff plan for pilot

Agenda for kickoff call (45 min):
- Introductions & roles (5m)
- Success criteria confirmation (10m)
- Trial plan & responsibilities (10m)
- Tech-deep-dive scheduling + access checklist (10m)
- Next steps & calendar (10m)

Proposed kickoff slots (all PT):
- Tue 12/16 10:00–10:45
- Wed 12/17 11:00–11:45
- Thu 12/18 15:00–15:45

Attachments: draft trial_charter_v1.docx (charter + success criteria) and a prompt_pack_template.json (sample prompt set for eval) — see attached stubs. Also linking REDWOOD SLA factsheet for your security team.

Can you please: 1) confirm which slot works, 2) who should join from your side (technical lead, product owner, CISO or procurement if needed), and 3) whether we should include procurement on the first call or handle contracting in parallel?

If none of the above windows work, send 2-3 alternatives and we’ll match. I’ll follow up to lock the calendar and create a shared Drive space for prompt packs and test data.

Thanks — look forward to getting this moving.

—

1) Ask size + exec summary: please flag any latency outliers you already see in production (example queries / 95th/99th percentile numbers). That helps us reproduce the profile during baseline runs.
2) Duration: the kickoff is best at 45 min as Tessa proposed, but please expect a follow-on 60–90m tech deep-dive within the first week for environment access and kernel/quantization tuning.
3) Sample prompts/data: the prompt_pack_template.json is attached as a starting point. If you can’t share masked data ahead of time, we can run with synthetic data and validate after the secure share comes through.

I’ve attached prompt_pack_template.json and will upload a short runbook after the kickoff. Also looping Marissa for renewal/opportunity tracking and to capture procurement contact details for contract cadence.
